speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your chest pain and vomiting, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
I need to see if there are any signs of pneumomediastinum or subcutaneous emphysema.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation

speaker: Patient
text: point. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That assessment is inconsistent with the clinical picture of forceful vomiting followed by chest pain, which strongly suggests a Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). I must request a contrast esophagogram or CT chest with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis, as a chest X-ray alone may be insufficient to detect the tear.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for Lyme disease, currently being treated with doxycycline. Social history: Reported alcohol use; found next to an empty bottle of vodka.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CT_chest_with_oral_contrast
This is critical to rule out esophageal rupture given the history of forceful vomiting and subsequent chest pain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CT and the history of doxycycline use followed by forceful retching, I suspect doxycycline-induced esophagitis or a small contained leak not seen on initial imaging. REQUEST TEST: Esophagogram_with_water_soluble_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal imaging results make esophageal rupture highly unlikely, so I must reconsider the diagnosis given the doxycycline history and alcohol use. REQUEST TEST: Upper_Endoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural causes like esophageal rupture or severe esophagitis have been ruled out by normal imaging and endoscopy, I need to explore other etiologies for your symptoms. Do you have any history of pancreatitis, gallstones, or recent trauma to your abdomen or chest?

speaker: Patient
text: Patient appears toxic and in acute distress, unable to provide a comprehensive review of systems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Amylase_and_Lipase
The patient's toxicity and history of heavy alcohol consumption strongly suggest acute pancreatitis, so I need to check these enzyme levels immediately.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Not specified

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the pancreatic enzymes were not specified, I must broaden the differential to include life-threatening thoracic conditions. REQUEST TEST: CT_Angiography_of_the_chest

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Pancreatitis
